name: Workflow gate nudge
description:
Decision gates declared in workflow_*.md files are treated as innate-tier
hard pauses. The regulator does not allow the work to cross a phase boundary
without explicit operator approval of that phase's gate criteria.

Origin: an autonomous multi-vertical predeployment session scaffolded
multiple Phase deliverables of a workflow_*.md without firing any of
the workflow's own declared decision gates. The gates were WRITTEN but
never ENFORCED. Operator then had to backfill review of dozens of
unchecked decision items across the deliverable set.

This rule treats workflow-declared gates as enforceable to prevent
recurrence.

trigger.detection_logic:
The hypothalamic-axis skill calls lib/workflow_gates.surface_workflow_gates()
on operator message + project memory. If a workflow file is in play AND its
gates have been parsed, the regulator tracks which phase the work is at.
When work attempts to advance to a phase whose entry-gate hasn't been
approved, this rule fires.

Phase tracking heuristics (v1 — coarse):
  - Operator says "phase 1 complete" / "phase 2 ready" / "moving to phase N"
    → mark phase N gate as needing approval before phase N+1 work begins
  - Phase name appears in observation-event details
  - Operator explicitly approves: "approve <phase> gate"

failure_mode_prevented.description:
Phase-boundary gate skipping. Producing 8 deliverables × 2 verticals
of unreviewed work, then asking operator to backfill review.
failure_mode_prevented.cost:
Operator must read every deliverable cold to verify the autonomous
work didn't drift from their preferences. The original purpose of
decision gates is to interleave operator approval with autonomous
work so review is incremental, not retrospective.
